Queen's egg sack inner layer - incorrect texture orientation

The inner layer is textured with strips (descriptors 112-147 on page 1, the same strips as
L263LEV's 310-345 on page 4), each strip a row of one picture, laid ring after ring along the
sack. In L263LEV the next strip is always at the bottom edge of the texture (219 of 220 cases).
In L391LEV 246 of the inner faces had their texture turned a quarter-turn, so the strips ran
around the sack instead of into each other.

Each fix rotates the face's four vertex indices (16 bytes at the face's offset); the texture
index, flag and light bytes are unchanged, as is the face's winding.

Texture orientation - faces from the texture scan review

These faces had their texture turned or mirrored so it did not run on from the faces next to it.
Each was found by ALTLevelScan, rendered before and after, and kept after review (Edward, 2026).

A turn rotates the face's four vertex indices (16 bytes at the face's offset), so the face keeps
its winding. A mirror swaps the flag byte (offset + 0x12) for its mirrored partner: 0 and 2,
4 and 6, 12 and 34, 8 and 10, 26 and 28, 30 and 32. The texture index and light bytes are
unchanged.

Face	Offset		Scan	Change	Was					Now
674	0xEA9C	391-2	three quarter-turns	3329, 3334, 3363, 3361	->	3361, 3329, 3334, 3363
2192	0x16134	391-1	a half-turn	4518, 4612, 4508, 4509	->	4508, 4509, 4518, 4612
2652	0x18524	391-3	a quarter-turn	4523, 4505, 4503, 4614	->	4505, 4503, 4614, 4523

==== Every patch to this file, in bytes (made from ALTEngine/data/Patches.json) ====
Offsets are into the file after the duplicate model removals (Patch/DUPLICATE-MODELS.txt), as the install applies them.
Each line: offset: shipped bytes -> patched bytes. To undo a patch, write the shipped bytes back.
